summary: Abbaas (RA) reports that Umar (RA) appeared to him in a dream after his death and said his reckoning was over and that only Allaah's mercy saved him.
Abbaas (RA) reports that after a year of du'aa he saw Umar (RA) in a dream, and Umar said his reckoning was over and that he was saved by a Forgiving and Merciful Rabb.
Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that after a year of du'aa he saw Umar (RA) in a dream, and Umar said he had found a Most Forgiving and Merciful Rabb.
Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that in a dream he saw a palace belonging to his father Umar (RA), who said he had been saved by a Forgiving Rabb and had just come back from his reckoning.
Saalim bin Abdullaah reports an Ansaari's account of seeing Umar (RA) in a dream after ten years, when Umar said his reckoning was complete and he was saved only by his Rabb's mercy.
notes: The Ansaari who had the dream is unnamed and left out.

summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) reports that in a dream Umar (RA) nudged his sleeping wife awake, and that he chased Umar and caught up only after exhausting himself, which Umar said was not due to his speed.
notes: Ummu Kulthoom bint Uqba is entered by name. The approved ummu-kulthoom may be the same person; check before merging.

summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) reports that Salmaan (RA) promised to visit him in a dream after death, and in the dream Salmaan told him to hold fast to Tawakkul.
A second report has Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) asking Salmaan (RA) in a dream which deed he found most virtuous, and Salmaan answering Tawakkul.

Auf bin Maalik (RA) reports seeing in a dream a tent belonging to Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, who said it was given for the Qur'aan and that Allaah had prepared a reward for Abu Dardaa because he pushed the world away.

Abdullaah bin Amr bin Haraam (RA) reports that Mubashir bin Abdul Mundhir told him in a dream that the martyrs of Badr live in Jannah, and the Prophet ﷺ remarked that this is the reality of martyrdom.
notes: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Haraam is entered by name. The approved abdullaah-bin-amr is not him, as far as the id shows. Mubashir is not in the approved list.

summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) says that the Sahabah found good in hardships, such as leaving Makkah with the Prophet ﷺ and the march to Badr, and cites the Qur'aan's account of Badr.
Ibn Ishaq narrates Abu Bakr's letter to Khaalid bin Waleed after Yamaamah, ordering him to march to Iraq and urging the Muslims to fight in Allaah's path with patience and sincerity.
notes: The letter is quoted in full; the closing sentence refers to earlier chapters.

summary: Utba bin Abd (RA) reports that the Sahabah pledged to fight with the Prophet ﷺ, and Ali (RA) rebuked an astrologer (Musaafir) for claiming to foresee harm on a journey, then marched at the hour he forbade and won at Nahrwaan.
notes: Musaafir is treated as a name for the astrologer. Moosa here is the Prophet Moosa, cited in a quotation.

summary: Taariq bin Ziyaad reports that Umar (RA) waded across water in humility, and when Abu Ubaydah objected, Umar said honour comes only through Islaam.
notes: Three variant reports of the same incident run together ('Another narration', 'Yet another narration'). Taariq bin Ziyaad is not in the approved list.

summary: Qais and Abul Aaliya Shaami report that Umar (RA) entering Shaam declined a Turkish horse and fine clothing, keeping his own camel and simple dress because Islaam gave him honour.
notes: Two separate reports (Qais, then Abul Aaliya) run together. Neither narrator is matched to an approved id. The head priest is unnamed and left out.

summary: Abu Nuhayk and Abdullaah bin Handhala report that they beat a man who reviled Maryam and Isa while they recited Surah Maryam, and Salmaan (RA) rebuked them and taught respect for others' beliefs and nafl salaah.
notes: Abu Nuhayk is not matched to an approved id (abu-nujayh is a different name). The man who was beaten is unnamed.

summary: Jubayr bin Nufayr (RA) reports seeing Abu Dardaa (RA) weeping after Cyprus was conquered, saying that the people were degraded because they forsook Allaah's commands and became obsessed with enslaving others.
notes: A second report ('Another narration') adds Abu Dardaa's words about enslaving others.

summary: Ibn Abu Maryam reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) told Umar (RA) that sincerity, salaah and obedience to the leader keep the Ummah steady, and later foretold that Umar would live only a short while.
notes: Ibn Abu Maryam is not matched to an approved id.

summary: Abu Abdah Ambari reports that after Madaa'in was conquered a man brought a dish of jewels to the booty, refusing praise out of fear of Allaah, and was identified as Aamir bin Abd Qays.
notes: Aamir bin Abd Qays and Abu Abdah Ambari are not in the approved list; Companion status unsure.

summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) and Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) vouch for the integrity of the army at Qaadisiyyah, and Jaabir names three men they had doubted, Tulayha, Amr bin Ma'dikarib and Qais bin Makshooh, who proved trustworthy and abstinent.
notes: Two separate reports (Sa'd, then Jaabir). The isnad names 'Hadhrat Muhammad', Talha and Muhajlab are left out as reference-line names. Tulayha is matched to the approved tulayha-bin-khuwaylid, not the Asadi entry.

summary: Qais Ijli reports that when the Persian emperor's sword, belt and jewels were brought to Umar (RA), Umar praised the trustworthiness of those who brought them, and Ali (RA) replied that the subjects are trustworthy because the ruler is.
notes: Qais Ijli is not matched to an approved id. The Persian emperor is unnamed.

summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports Umar's letter to Amr bin al-Aas urging him to seek Allaah's help with sincere intentions and prayer, and a later letter sending four thousand reinforcements under commanders including Zubayr, Miqdaad, Ubaadah and Maslamah.
notes: Two separate reports: the letter to Amr, and the reinforcement letter ('Another narration'). Maslamah bin Mukhallad is not in the approved list.

summary: Iyaadh Ash'ari reports that at Yarmook five commanders shared the army with Abu Ubaydah as commander-in-chief, and the army wrote to Umar (RA) that the enemy outnumbered them and asked for reinforcements.
notes: Two different Iyaadhs appear: the narrator (Iyaadh Ash'ari) and the other commander, entered as 'Iyaadh'. Neither is in the approved list.

summary: Umar (RA) replies to the army's request for reinforcements by directing them to Allaah, who helped Muhammad ﷺ at Badr when his forces were fewer than theirs.
Umar (RA) adds that the army should fight without writing back, and after victory Iyaadh (RA) proposed exchanging ten prisoners for each Muslim, while Abu Ubaydah (RA) raced a youngster who beat him.
notes: Continues the account from n03784 and opens with 'Another narration'. The Iyaadh here is probably the same commander as in n03783, but that is not confirmed. The youngster is unnamed.

summary: After Zuhr, Sa'd (RA) had a young Qaari recite Surah Anfaal to the army at Qaadisiyyah, and the whole army learned it and drew tranquillity from it; another report says he ordered them to recite it to one another.
notes: The isnad names (Muhammad, Talha, Ziyaad) are left out as reference-line names. The young reciter is unnamed. A second report ('Another narration') is included.

summary: Ibraheem bin Haarith Tameemi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a force with instructions to recite Surah Mu'minoon verse 115 every morning and evening, and they gained booty and remained safe.
notes: Ibraheem bin Haarith Tameemi is not matched to an approved id (ibraheem-taymi is not sahabi and is a different person).

summary: Sa'd (RA) commands the Muslims to hold position until after Zuhr, call Allaahu Akbar with each of his calls, and finally charge while reciting 'Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Illaa Billaah'.
notes: The heading says 'Battle of Badr', but the narration does not name the battle; it is the Qaadisiyyah context. The isnad names (Muhammad, Talha, Ziyaad) are left out.

summary: Sa'd (RA) calls the Takbeer three times while the Qurraa finish reciting the verses of Jihaad, the army mobilises, and the most courageous go forward; the narration is cut off.
notes: Ends mid-narration ('The narration still continues further'). It is a variant of the account in n03788.

summary: Ja'far bin Abdullaah bin Hakam reports that Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) kept a hat containing hairs of the Prophet ﷺ taken at Umrah, and was granted victory whenever he wore it into battle.
notes: A second, shorter report ('Another narration') is included. Ja'far bin Abdullaah bin Hakam is not in the approved list.

summary: Shaqeeq reports that at Qaadisiyyah, when the muadhin was injured, the Sahabah eagerly competed to call the adhaan, and Sa'd (RA) settled it by drawing lots.
notes: Shaqeeq is not matched to an approved id (abu-waail-shaqeeq-bin-salama is a different person). The muadhin is unnamed.

summary: Ma'qal bin Yasaar (RA) reports the conquest of Isfahaan, where Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) went as envoy to the Persian ruler Dhul Haajibayn, and Mughiera contrasted the Arabs' former poverty and the Prophet's message with the Persian splendour.
notes: Ends mid-narration ('The narration still continues further').

summary: Rib'ee bin Aamir, Hudhayfah bin Mihsin and Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) each go before Rustam at Qaadisiyyah in turn; they reject the Persian display of wealth and call the Persians to Islaam, Jizya or battle.
notes: Contains several episodes, and the Mughiera episode is a separate report ('Another narration'). The narration is also cut off at the end. The isnad names (Muhammad, Talha, Amr, Ziyaad) are left out. The Persian courtiers are unnamed.

summary: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that at Mu'ta, daunted by the enemy's numbers, he was reminded by Thaabit bin Aqram (RA) that victory comes through Allaah, not through large numbers.
notes: Thaabit bin Aqram is not matched to an approved id; check against thaabit and arqam before merging.

summary: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports Abu Bakr's letter to Amr bin Al Aas that victory never depended on numbers, recalling Uhud and the scarce horses and camels of the Prophet's time, and urging obedience to Allaah.
notes: Matched to the approved abdullaah-bin-amr on the assumption that the book's 'bin Amr bin Al Aas' is that person; the approved list does not spell out the father.

summary: Ubaadah (RA) and Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) report that Khaalid answered a man who feared the Romans' numbers by saying Muslims win through Allaah's help, not numbers, and wished the Romans were double.
notes: Ubaadah is not matched to an approved id. The Yarmook companion may be Ubaadah bin Saamit, but that is not confirmed. The man is unnamed.

summary: Zuhri reports that after some Arabs apostatised, Abu Bakr sent Khaalid bin Waleed, who defeated the false prophet Tulayha, and one of Tulayha's own men said his side fought people who wanted to die before their companions.
notes: Ends mid-narration ('The narration still goes on'). Ukaasha bin Mihsin and Ibn Aqram are not matched to approved ids. Tulayha is matched to the Asadi entry, which is marked (?).

summary: Amr bin Al Aas (RA) reports his conversation with the king of Alexandria, in which he described the Arabs' former state and the Prophet's message, and the king advised that they would prevail only while they followed their prophet's teachings.
notes: The king of Alexandria is unnamed and left out.

summary: Abu Is'haaq reports that Heraclius asked why his defeated Roman army lost to Muslims who pray at night, fast by day and keep promises, and an elderly leader replied that the Romans drank, fornicated and oppressed.
notes: Heraclius is not in the approved list. The elderly leader is unnamed.

summary: Yahya bin Yahya Ghassaani reports that two Arab Christians spied on the Muslims at Damascus and described them as monks by night, horsemen by day, always reciting the Qur'aan and making dhikr, and the Damascus commander said they could not be resisted.
notes: The two men and the commander of Damascus are unnamed and left out. Yahya bin Yahya Ghassaani is not in the approved list.
